newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar launches its third fertiliser complex.
newsitem.headline: Qatar launches its third fertiliser complex.

text.p: Qatar's Emir, Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa al-Thani, on Monday commissioned the country's third fertiliser complex, making it the Middle East's largest producer of chemical fertilisers in the Middle East, officials said.
Built at a cost of $540 million, QAFCO III was designed to produce 1,500 tonnes of ammonia and 2,000 tonnes of urea a day.
Qatar Fertilizer Company Ltd (QAFCO) already has two plants in operation with a combined output of 2,300 tonnes of ammonia and 2,500 tonnes of urea a day.

Addressing a gathering at the commissioning ceremony at Messaieed, 48 km (30 miles) south of the capital Doha, Minister of Energy and Industry Abdullah bin Hamad al-Attiyah, said: "QAFCO will now be able to export up to 400,000 tonnes of ammonia gas liquids and 1.5 million tonnes of urea annually".
Ammonia is the raw material used to produce urea. One tonne of ammonia mixed with carbon dioxide, produces two tonnes of urea.
QAFCO is 75 percent owned by the state Qatar General Petroleum Corp and 25 percent by Norway's Norsk Hydro ASA.
